**IW-5. Reading source: one pull per instrument per frame; never cache; never read truth.**
*Rule.* In the render callback each on-screen instrument in a loaded section obtains its displayed value with exactly one `perceived(ref, viewer)` call (PF-7), `viewer` being the local seat's `PlayerId`; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* one **`InstrumentPresenter` per instrument** is the sole caller of `perceived()` for its ref and the sole owner of the settle, tremor, dwell and notch scalars, and the wall node and the card are views of the frame index and digits it publishes once per frame (the Filter's `(ref, viewer, frame)` memo is the backstop; ADR candidate, X-6). An instrument never stores a `Perceived` record across frames, never addresses the Filter by `peer_id` (PF-10), and never calls `true_value`, `summary()` (a ship-status read), `power_use()` (Attention's stimulus) or `can_join()`. It may read `read_view` only for **non-value** inputs: the tremor predicate (IW-12), module frame selection and WORN (IW-17, IW-18), the alarm predicate (IW-19), and binding validity (IW-30). Those reads are refreshed once per Graph step (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6), not per frame, and never feed a displayed value. The needle target is `displayed_pm`. An instrument that is off-screen or in an unloaded section pulls nothing; on its first pull after being culled it **snaps** to `displayed_pm` with no settle and no interpolation from stale history (history older than one Graph step is meaningless, and a settle on re-entry would be a motion with no world cause, P1) (advisor ruling R18).
*Why.* PF-8: the record never contains the truth while a lie is active; caching would let a stale record outlive a lie's end. R18 and PF-3: only the Filter wraps a true value.
*Edge notes.* Presentation-local scalars (the settle triple, `prev_honest_pm` and the rest, window and reversal-dwell scalars of IW-11, tremor onset and decay timestamps, the numeral throttle timestamp) are derived drawing state, not cached `Perceived` records: each is a pure function of values the player was already shown, none is read by another system, all are discarded on restore, cull and camera cut. **CONFLICT K-17 (new): LSG:998 and LS-20 (LSG:201) (locked) say "gauges read `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles" (LS-20: "Instruments and Audio poll `read_view` at render rate for smooth needles")**, which contradicts R18/PF-3 (a gauge never reads a value from `read_view`). This GDD follows R18 and PF-3: value reads go only through `perceived`; the "smooth needles" of LSG:998 and LS-20 is delivered by IW-11's interpolation, not by a value read. The Graph's own sentences are routed to its owner as a refresh. Related: the honest path carries no previous value, which IW-11 answers with the local scalar `prev_honest_pm` (K-17, checkpoint ruling C14).

======
### D.5 Tremor (`tremor_offset`)

The tremor offset formula is defined as:

`s(t) = 0.6 * sin(2 * pi * f1 * t + phi1) + 0.4 * sin(2 * pi * f2 * t + phi2)`, `t = present_time`; `f_1 = 6.0 + 1.5 * u_1` (6.0 .. 7.5 Hz) and `f_2 = 9.0 + 1.0 * u_2` (9.0 .. 10.0 Hz), two **disjoint sub-bands** of the 6-10 Hz tremor band, so `f_2 - f_1` >= 1.5 Hz and the beat period is at most 0.67 s *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (the earlier shared band let about 12 % of instruments draw near-equal frequencies and so long or permanent null windows with no tremor); `(u_i, phi_i)` from a presentation-local stateless hash of `(ref_key, i)`

`A_eff = max( TREMOR_AMP_PX, ceil( TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k ) )`

`env(t) = min(1, (t - t_on) / TREMOR_ONSET_MS)` while `p_eff` holds; `env_off x max(0, 1 - (t - t_off) / TREMOR_DECAY_MS)` after it ends, with `env_off` = `env(t_off)` **latched at the instant the predicate ends** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (the earlier decay branch started from 1.0, so a predicate pulse that ended mid-onset jumped the envelope up to full before decaying); `p_eff = predicate OR (t - t_last_true) < TREMOR_HOLD_S`

`o = clamp( round( TREMOR_GAIN * A_eff * env * s(t) ), -A_eff, +A_eff )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, **in frame-index space** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `o` is a number of pre-rendered needle frames (OQ-IW-7: one frame index is one tip pixel along the arc, or one meniscus row of a LINEAR glass), and the drawn index is `idx_drawn = clamp( idx_base + o, 0, N_idx - 1 )` with `idx_base` the settle or ramp base index and `N_idx` the frame count of the sheet, so a non-zero `o` always moves the drawn tip by exactly `o` indices (the earlier tangent offset in art px could round to the same tip pixel on about 9 % of frames at 45 degrees) and the sum can never leave the end stops. The angular equivalent is `o x arc_deg / (N_idx - 1)` degrees

(The two-sine sum is wanted here: PF D.4 rejected it for the **wander** because a beat that dips to rest would break never-rest, whereas tremor has no never-rest duty and its irregularity is the point; a dip to rest between bursts reads as a real needle on a shaking hull.)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TREMOR_F_MIN_HZ`, `TREMOR_F_MAX_HZ` | float Hz | 6 and 10 (named here from ART 7.3, not new) | art bible | the tremor band; disjoint from the Filter's 0.40-0.45 Hz wander; the two sines draw from the sub-bands 6.0-7.5 and 9.0-10.0 Hz inside it | *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)*
| `u_i`, `phi_i` | float | [0, 1), [0, 2 pi) | a presentation hash of `ref_key` (PF D.14 is the precedent; ADR candidate); **never** the kernel `rng_derive`, sim RNG is never used for presentation | per-instrument frequencies and phases, so two trembling gauges do not move in step |
| `TREMOR_AMP_PX` | int art px | 1 (ART 7.3 +-1), range 1-2 | this GDD | amplitude in art px |
| `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` | int screen px | 2 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 2-3 | this GDD | the HR-12 floor applied to tremor |
| `k` | int | 1..`k_auto`+2 | PIPE zoom ladder | world scale |
| `TREMOR_GAIN` | float | 1.5 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, range 1.2-2.0 | this GDD | gain per unit of `A_eff` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: at `A_eff` 1, abs(o) = 1 when abs(s) >= 0.33; at `A_eff` 2, abs(o) = 1 when abs(s) >= 0.167 and 2 when abs(s) >= 0.5 |
| `TREMOR_ONSET_MS`, `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` | int ms | 150 (100-300), 600 (300-1000) `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | envelope; on a re-rise during a decay `t_on := t - env x TREMOR_ONSET_MS` so `env` stays continuous |
| `TREMOR_HOLD_S` | float s | 0 (range 0-1.0) `[PLACEHOLDER]` | this GDD | the playtest remedy if the predicate flaps at Graph-step rate |
| `predicate` | bool | | IW-12, refreshed per Graph step | true only while `motion_mode` is HONEST and a physical stress cause holds |

**Output Range:** `o` is an integer in [-`A_eff`, +`A_eff`]; 0 once the predicate has been false for `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`; exactly 0 in every non-HONEST frame. `A_eff` is 2 art px at `k` 1 and 1 art px at every `k` >= 2, so the offset is at least `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` screen px at every rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (reachable now that the gain scales with `A_eff`: the earlier unscaled gain reached 2 only at abs(s) = 1, so the k=1 tremor was effectively 1 px and the HR-12 floor claim was false). **Tremor and wander stay distinct:** wander peaks at 2 art px at 0.35-0.45 Hz, tremor at `A_eff` (1 art px at every `k` >= 2) at 6-10 Hz. At `k` 1 the peaks are equal (2 art px) and the cue is frequency and flip rate (tremor 12-20 tip flips per second against the wander's 4-6, VA-6); that is an accepted limitation of the zoom-out rung, recorded as OQ-IW-41. **Activity lint (`TREMOR_ACTIVITY`)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: measured on the **drawn tip index**, not on `o`: for every manifest `ref_key`, in any 2 s window at `env` 1, the drawn index changes between consecutive render frames at least `TREMOR_TIP_CHANGE_MIN_HZ` times per second (8 `[PLACEHOLDER]`, set by a measured sweep of the manifest `ref_key`s; the value must stay above the wander's 4-6 flips per second by a non-overlap margin, so the cue stays flip rate, OQ-IW-41) at `A_eff` 1 and at `A_eff` 2; a failing `ref_key` takes the next `tremor_salt` in its record. (The earlier lint counted frames with abs(o) >= 1, a worst case of 46 % at `A_eff` 1 and 62 % at `A_eff` 2 in a sweep of 4000 random draws; that measured `o`, which is not what the player sees, and it is replaced.) **Short pulse:** a predicate that holds for 100 ms and ends has `env_off` = 100 / `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` = 0.67, the decay runs from 0.67 and `env` never exceeds 0.67 (AC-IW-121).

**Example:** `ref_key` hashes give `f1` 7.2 Hz, `f2` 9.1 Hz, `phi` 0. At `k` 3, `A_eff` = max(1, ceil(2/3)) = 1; mid-stress (`env` 1) at t = 0.050 s: `s` = 0.6 sin(2.262) + 0.4 sin(2.859) = 0.6 x 0.7705 + 0.4 x 0.2790 = 0.574; `o` = clamp(round(1.5 x 0.574 = 0.86), -1, 1) = +1 px. At `k` 1, `A_eff` = 2 and `o` = clamp(round(1.5 x 2 x 0.574 = 1.72), -2, 2) = +2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Decay: 300 ms after the predicate ends `env` = 0.5, so the product is at most 0.75 in magnitude and rounds to +-1 only when abs(s) >= 0.667, mostly 0; at 600 ms `env` = 0 and the needle rests on one pixel.

I'm working through a potential conflict in the tremor formula: the drawn tremor depends on a weight that starts at 1000 during honest states and decays toward 0 during a lie, with the envelope effectively suppressing new tremor outside the honest frame.

I'm deciding that the envelope should latch at its last honest-frame value rather than continuing to rise once the mode goes non-honest, so the weight decay alone produces the fade to zero — if the envelope was already decaying when the lie started, I'll just let it continue decaying on its own schedule multiplied by the falling weight.

On return to HONEST, the tremor state resets fully: once weight hits zero the presenter discards envelope and onset time, so a fresh tremor re-onsets with its own ramp if the predicate still holds, rather than resuming the old envelope. I also need to confirm weight only clears at zero and stays there until the next CLEAR, even if the lie itself ends sooner.

The tremor's underlying sine phase uses the same hash-based continuous timing across the HONEST/non-HONEST boundary, so there's no visible jump at onset — that's the whole point of the blend. The drawn offset gets rounded to an integer, scaled by weight, clamped to the effective amplitude, and added to the base needle position, which during a lie is the Filter's wandering trajectory rather than the plain honest value.

Under reduced motion the tremor isn't drawn at all, so the weight has nothing to blend — the notch pair just substitutes for it, shown while the predicate holds and cleared immediately on leaving HONEST, matching the Filter's rule that settle triples and notches clear instantly. The card mirrors this same tremor behavior with the same weighting (parity with IW-26), and the predicate for starting a new tremor is only sampled while in HONEST, though a running tremor can continue blending out afterward.

Now I need to trace the invariant changes: SETTLING should imply HONEST, while the TREMOR flag should imply either HONEST or a non-HONEST fading sub-state where tremor_weight_pm is still positive from a tremor that was already running. The DEAD state stays tremor-free. I also need to update the table entry describing TREMOR flag exit conditions and the FILTER_DRIVEN rule — tremor can't be *started* there, but a fading tremor carried over from HONESTY should still be allowed to decay through FILTER_DRIVEN. There are likely many other spots in the spec asserting "no tremor outside HONEST" that need similar fixes, so I should grep for every "tremor" mention across the invariants and acceptance criteria to catch them all.

== L200
Housing glow frames (the lamp lit/unlit pair) and the pip (IW-4) ride the `HOUSING_GLOW` ref (stage 2). The stage-1 "readout" of SN-16 is the card's numeral, which is `displayed_value` of the `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (the digit tick of PF-18 acts there; TICK and STALE govern the numeral only, IW-13); it is not a second lie surface. A wall gauge carries no digit. The SN-16 "readout" wording is routed to Sanity and the `motion_mode` field description and PF-18 to the Filter as a wording refresh (checkpoint ruling C2).
== L220
*Rule.* Per instrument surface, a record in `assets/data/instruments/`: `instrument_id`; `gauge_kind` (DIAL | LINEAR | READOUT | GLYPH | FRAME); `size_class`; `quantity` (IW-9); `arc_deg` (DIAL; 0 for LINEAR); `needle_len_px` (DIAL) or `travel_px` (LINEAR meniscus travel); `value_lo`, `value_hi`, `lsb`, `unit_key`, `name_key` (the card label); `zones[]` as LS-7 band **names** mapped to a pattern class (D.2; the thresholds are derived at build time and never written into this data); `lie_surface_id` per corruptible surface (`<instrument_id>.needle`, `.glyph`, `.housing_glow`, `.machine_frame`; there is no `.readout` surface and the card has no id of its own: one ref carries one lie and one `Perceived`, so the card numeral is `displayed_value` of the `.needle` ref's `Perceived`, and `motion_mode` TICK and STALE apply to that numeral, checkpoint ruling C2); and `beyond_witness`, the flag set defined below, which is **derived from placement and quantity** and must equal the authored value (lint `BEYOND_WITNESS_MISMATCH`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The binding (`node_ref` or `room_key`, `mount`, `host_face` and, since the design review, `mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node`) is **placement data** authored in Layout and Derelict Authoring (IW-31). A missing or malformed record yields the honest path plus `lie_unrenderable` (PF-44), a **build failure** for any kind listed in `lie_targets.json`. Assets owed exactly as PF V.11: `mach_gauge_<loop>_alb.png` plus `_msk.png` with slices `glass`, `needle_edge`, `needle`; a `ui_` sheet with a `glass` slice for digit cells and card glass; `mach_<name>_<state>_alb.png`; `mach_lamp_<name>_lit` / `_unlit`; both honest state frames of every pair on **one sheet page** (advisor ruling R11; PF-45). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, answers Perception Filter PF-9 join)* **Join to Sanity's `subject_ref` `{stable_id, surface}` (SN-23).** `stable_id` is the module's stable id and equals the IW-8 `instrument_id` (lint: one-to-one). The surface enum maps to the facets above: 1 NEEDLE maps to `.needle`; 2 READOUT maps to the `.needle` facet of an instrument whose `gauge_kind` is READOUT (a digit-only instrument has no needle sprite, but its single lie facet is that ref, whose `displayed_value` is the numeral); 3 GLYPH to `.glyph`; 4 GLOW_SPRITE to `.housing_glow`; 5 MACHINE_SPRITE to `.machine_frame`. The ref's `quantity`, `node_ref` or `room_key` come from this record, never from the `subject_ref`. The record supplies both an OK and an alarm interval (PF-45) so the Filter can derive the GLIDE dial side. Lint
== L396
*Rule.* With reduced motion (HR-8): honest settle becomes a **step** (drawn = `displayed_pm`); honest tremor is replaced by a **held stress notch pair** (each `max(NOTCH_PAIR_PX, ceil(NOTCH_MIN_SCREEN_PX / k))` art px, at least 4 screen px at every rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), shown while the IW-12 predicate holds **and** `motion_mode` is HONEST, and never on a lying reading (it would be an oracle); the alarm mark holds solid. Glide, wander and lying-tick scaling are the Filter's (PF-39: `RM_GLIDE_SCALE` 0.6, rate floor not below 0.3 deg/s, wander never scaled, lying tick never below `LIE_TICK_MS`) and are not restated. The notch is two Void Steel nicks cut into the world bezel's top edge about 4 px either side of centre, and, on the card, two Hull Grey squares on the Ground plate above the dial *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's placement adopted; R19 said "on the bezel", but HR-2 forbids Hull Grey on a bezel fill, so the card's notch sits on the Ground side of the dial rim)*. No setting removes a leak mode, hides the gleam or the card numeral, or adds an Attention or sanity surface. Instrument labels and the card obey the 21/15 text tier and UI scale `H`; the instrument face is a bitmap font at integer `H` only (advisor ruling R19). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* **Reduce flashing defaults ON at first launch** (user ruling, D79): the card's honest numeral already rides the shared hold grid (D.3) and adds no flash surface that the default would need to suppress; under the HUD's stricter arbiter for reduce flashing (HS-47) a grid boundary may be skipped and the card shows the then-latest step at the next one, which the lag bound of `2 x HONEST_TICK_MS` already covers. Card tremor is suppressed under `reduced_motion` (IW-12, D96).
== L466
*Rule.* In development builds only, each instrument exposes a read-only `drawn_value(ref)` (the value it actually drew this frame, answering the Debug Overlay's render-probe ask DO-22, whose `DEFECT_BYPASS` class detects a corruptible node that skipped the Filter) and an `instrument_diag(ref)` record `{instrument_id, ref_key, motion_mode as drawn, settle_active, tremor_active, card_open, state}`. Both are tagged dev-only and stripped from release builds; neither is a value source for any gameplay or presentation node; neither exposes `true_value` (the Overlay calls that itself, DIAGNOSTIC). Instruments publish a stable integer `ref_key` per instrument (the Filter's, PF-9) and keep four counters for the Overlay and the lints: `diag.instr_pm_clamped` (a `displayed_pm` outside 0..1000 was clamped), `diag.inspect_unresolved` (IW-24), `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` (IW-16). The Overlay treats an absent probe as `bypass_check: ABSENT`, never clean (DO-22). In development builds only, Instruments registers one diagnostics channel at composition-root time under the Debug Overlay's channel contract (DO-12, `diag_panel_contract`), carrying the counters `diag.instr_pm_clamped`, `diag.inspect_unresolved`, `diag.instr_quantity_collision` and `diag.gleam_over_cap` and the `instrument_diag(ref)` rows. The channel is a dev-only panel registration, not a kernel block, hook, mutator or dirty key, so IW-2's zero-registration rule is unchanged; it is stripped from release builds.
== L498
`ALARM` is set while an `alarm_eligible` `FailureDescriptor` exists on the bound subject (read through `failures(filter)`, refreshed per Graph step) and cleared with it. It is orthogonal to every state above and to `motion_mode`: a lying needle never sets, moves or clears it. Only the Graph causes it (LS-13 fairness gate). It is drawn only on housings that carry the mark (IW-19) and never on the card.
== L569
1. **Perception Filter, I-B row (PF:556).** "*In-World Instruments & Inspect View (Hard dependent) | `perceived(ref, viewer)` -> `Perceived` (PF-8) for needle, readout, glyph, housing, machine frame; the gleam amplitude and the leak-material parameters; the `motion_mode` | the PF-45 calibration record in the tag; a separate pivoted needle of at least 16 art px; a `_msk` glass and needle-edge slice; both honest state frames on one sheet page; honest settle and tremor **only** when `motion_mode` is HONEST; the card is the same ref as the wall gauge; the card drawn only when its instrument is lit | Instruments own the needle sprite, digit mechanism, settle and tremor, the card. The Filter owns the lie trajectory and its return.*" **Accepted** (IW-7, IW-8, IW-10, IW-11, IW-12, IW-13, IW-17, IW-26, IW-24). One amendment: PF's "readout" is the card numeral only, `displayed_value` of the needle's own ref and not a separate ref (IW-6, checkpoint ruling C2); the wording refresh is routed to the Filter and to Sanity. Also PF-45 ("Instruments also owe: a pivoted needle as a separate sprite or slice, a `_msk` slice naming the glass and needle-edge regions the gleam uses, both honest state frames on one sheet page, and the honest settle applied only when `motion_mode` is HONEST") is **answered** by IW-8; PF-18 (the card lies exactly when the gauge lies; violet only on the reading's glass) by IW-16 and IW-26; PF UI Requirements (never cache a `Perceived`, never apply settle or tremor to a non-HONEST reading, never address the Filter by `peer_id`) by IW-5 and IW-13.
== L601
`pm_draw = pm_honest` (HONEST, no settle) `| settle_response(from_pm, to_pm, t_jump)` (HONEST, a jump, D.4) `| displayed_pm` (every other `motion_mode`, verbatim)
== L927
`notch_on = reduced_motion AND stress_predicate AND (motion_mode == HONEST)`
== L1253
| Three motions: settle, tremor, glide; honest = cause, mass, rest; lie = none of these | ART 7.3 | VA-6; settle and tremor only when `motion_mode` is HONEST |
== L1349
* **Stress notch (IW-27).** World: two Void Steel nicks, each `max(2, ceil(4 / k))` art px square (2x2 at `k` 2 and above, 4x4 at `k` 1: at least 4 screen px at every rung) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, cut into the bezel top edge about 4 px either side of centre. Card: two 2x2 Hull Grey squares (at least 6 screen px at `H_card` 3) on the Ground plate above the dial (HR-2 forbids Hull Grey on a bezel fill, so the card's notch sits on the Ground side of the dial rim; a minor deviation from R19's word "bezel"). Static while the IW-12 predicate holds and `motion_mode` is HONEST; absent on a lying reading; exactly as discriminating as tremor and no more.
== L1399
Motion rules (before any number): settle and tremor only when `motion_mode` is HONEST; a glide is Filter-driven (`displayed_pm` over time) and the instrument adds nothing but the Filter-supplied wander; no `Tween`, no wall clock; `present_time` closed forms, frozen under PAUSED; every placement is integer art px (PR-8).
== L1446
| E6 | Lie begins (Filter) | the needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim (slew plus wander) from the current drawn angle; the gleam fades up with `leak_amplitude_pm` | the Filter's `FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` (needle, card, glyph) or `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` (housing, machine), starting no later than the glide | corruptible | any settle or tremor on the lying instrument; a sound-only lie |
== L1482
| Stress notch, tremor | honest-only presentation of a Graph predicate | none (a `read_view` predicate) | never on a lying reading | none | absent when `motion_mode` is not HONEST |
== L1740
| PF-45: honest settle and tremor only when `motion_mode` is HONEST; a separate pivoted needle; a `_msk` glass and needle-edge slice; both honest state frames on one sheet page | IW-8, IW-10, IW-11, IW-12, IW-13, IW-17 |
== L1827
**New `[PLACEHOLDER]` constants to register now are the starred knobs of Tuning Knobs (`NEEDLE_LEN_MIN_PX` ownership, `DIAL_L_NEEDLE_PX`, `DIAL_S_NEEDLE_PX`, `DIAL_ARC_DEG`, `ZONE_MIN_ARC_PX`, `NEEDLE_SCREEN_MIN_PX`, `ALARM_MARK_WORLD_PX`, the four starred `INSTR_SETTLE_` constants (`ZETA`, `OMEGA`, `MS`, `JUMP_PM`; the unstarred `INSTR_REST_STEPS`, `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` and `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` replace the retired `INSTR_SETTLE_REST_PM`), `GLEAM_EDGE_SCREEN_MIN`, `LINEAR_TRAVEL_PX`, `D_VIS_MIN_PX`, `LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS`, `TRAVEL_MIN_PX`, `CARD_MAG`, `CARD_W_ART_PX` / `CARD_H_ART_PX`, `CARD_MAX_FRAC_H`, `INSTRUMENT_SHARE_MAX`); the unstarred knobs are local data, listed for completeness and registered only when a neighbour cites them. Tuning Knobs is the authority for the list and is checked against it name for name. Owned knob values, owner In-World Instruments, each with a safe range, a derivation and the too-high / too-low behaviour in Tuning Knobs:** `DIAL_L_NEEDLE_PX` 24, `DIAL_S_NEEDLE_PX` 18, `DIAL_ARC_DEG` 240, `NEEDLE_STROKE_ART_PX` 2, `ZONE_BAND_PX_L` 3, `ZONE_BAND_PX_S` 3, `ZONE_MIN_ARC_PX` 6, `NEEDLE_SCREEN_MIN_PX` 24, `INSTR_SETTLE_ZETA` 0.7, `INSTR_SETTLE_OMEGA` 20, `INSTR_SETTLE_MS` 400, `INSTR_SETTLE_JUMP_PM` 40, `INSTR_REST_STEPS` 3, `INSTR_SETTLE_WINDOW_STEPS` 4, `INSTR_REVERSAL_DWELL_STEPS` 4, `TREMOR_AMP_PX` 1, `TREMOR_MIN_SCREEN_PX` 2, `TREMOR_GAIN` 1.5, `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` 150, `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` 600, `TREMOR_SEV_MIN` 1, `TREMOR_HOLD_S` 0, `GLEAM_EDGE_SCREEN_MIN` 2, `PIP_PX` 4x2 (range 2x2-4x2), `TREMOR_F_MIN_HZ` 6 and `TREMOR_F_MAX_HZ` 10 (named here from ART 7.3, not new), `LINEAR_TRAVEL_PX` 50, `D_VIS_MIN_PX` 4, `LINEAR_GLIDE_RATE_MIN_PXS` 0.5, `TRAVEL_MIN_PX` 40, `ALARM_MARK_WORLD_PX` 16, `NOTCH_PAIR_PX` 2, `CARD_MAG` 1 (fixed, range 1-2), `CARD_W_ART_PX` / `CARD_H_ART_PX` 72 / 72, `CARD_MAX_FRAC_H` 0.5, `CARD_GAP_HUD_PX` 4, `CARD_KEEPOUT_CHEST_R` 28, `CARD_KEEPOUT_BEAM_HALFW` 12, `INSTRUMENT_SHARE_MAX` 24, `T_VIS_MAX_S` 3.2 (was 2.0; range 1.9-4, D.12). #### Group D. Lying surfaces, state frames and the alarm mark

**IW-16. The gleam is drawn here, on glass and edges only.**
*Rule.* Instruments draw the gleam from `Perceived.leak_amplitude_pm` and the Filter's phase: hue fringe `#B07BE6` (never the core `#8A3FD1`), at an **edge** only (glass edge, needle leading edge, housing edge), never a fill, peak channel at most `LEAK_MAX_CH` (:= `DECOY_MAX_CH` 0.85), produced at runtime by a material parameter or modulate and never baked into a sheet (reserved-hue scan, ART:1207). **World gauge:** on the instrument's own material by a per-instance parameter (zero added draws); *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **fallback if per-instance CanvasItem shader parameters are unavailable in 4.7.2 (`[UNV]`):** a child edge sprite per lying instrument, cut from the `_msk` edge slice, whose `modulate.a` carries the amplitude: no new ShaderMaterial (the LO-13 budget of five holds) and one extra draw per lying on-screen instrument (a pooled material per quantised amplitude is rejected because it would spend the material budget); the edge thickness requested is the effective art px of D.9 (`ceil(2/k)` clamped 1-2, so at least 2 screen px at every rung; inside the Filter's `[PLACEHOLDER]` `GLEAM_EDGE_PX` range 1-2, PF-16, OQ-IW-4). **Card (the answer to OQ-PF-11 / PF C-3 for the card):** Instruments draw the gleam on the card's glass and needle edge and the digit well's top and bottom edge, in HUD art px (1 HUD art px = `H` screen px, `H` >= 3, so HR-12's 2-screen-px stroke always holds), from the same amplitude and phase as the wall gauge. The card frame, bezel and rivets are an anchor and never carry violet (PF-18, SNV-8). Cut order if Filter spike S-1 fails: housing and glyph gleams first, **never** the needle or the card numeral well (PF-42's "never needle and readout") (advisor ruling R5).
*Why.* The Filter owns amplitude and phase but no layer-2 node; HUD & Suit Layer (designed in this run) supplies only the frame and the gleam helper; the card glass is Instruments' node.
*Edge notes.* **Hue risk (art-director finding).** A gleam multiplied by a coloured light leaves the violet band: `#B07BE6` under the beam core `#FFE2A8` shifts toward magenta (hue about 321 degrees, still inside 270-330), and under Chemlight `#86B896` it reads blue (about 244 degrees), darker. A lying gauge lit only by a glowstick would lose its hue mode. Requirement: the gleam is composited so its hue is not modulated by the light's colour (intensity gated by the host's lit factor, hue fixed) -> ADR candidate (shared with the Filter's spike S-1 and OQ-PF-6); the motion mode survives regardless and HR-5 needs only each mode sufficient, so this is a risk, not a break. Instance-parameter transport and batching are `[UNV]` HIGH risk.

**IW-17. The Module-Body Presenter.**
*Rule.* For each module sheet the Presenter selects one **honest** frame from the Graph state and, where tagged, from `perceived(MACHINE_FRAME | HOUSING_GLOW | STATE_GLYPH).frame_override`:

| Graph input (`node(id)`) | Honest frame from the sheet | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `state` 0 OK, `served_pm` > 0 | `running` | rotor / moving-medium region animates (pipe-side witnesses are Failure & Trail's and Lighting's; the *machine's own* medium is part of this frame) |
| `state` 0 OK, `served_pm` = 0 | `stopped` | idle, not failed |
| `state` 1 DEGRADED without a hazard mode (WORN) | `running` or `stopped` plus the wear overlay (IW-18) | no condition word, no bar |
| `state` 1 DEGRADED with a hazard mode (1-9) | `running` or `stopped` by `served_pm` exactly as state 0, plus the wear overlay; `cracked` only for housings and tanks whose live hazard is LEAK or BREACH; the lamp pair follows `served_pm` (lit while `served_pm` > 0) | the machine still functions at reduced `eff` (LS-10); no condition word, no bar |
| `state` 2 FAILED | `stopped` for pumps and rotors; `cracked` for housings and tanks | lamp pair `unlit` (no function, LS-10) |
| `state` 3 DESTROYED | `cracked` plus the dead frame | binding lost (IW-30) |
| `state` 4 SALVAGED, 5 ABSENT | module gone; no frame | |

`frame_override` swaps to the *other honest frame of the same pair* (running/stopped, whole/cracked, lamp lit/unlit); the Filter never supplies a frame the sheet lacks: SPRITE_SWAP eligibility is `has_both_frames(def_id, pair)`, **a requested Item DB query** that implements SN AC-SN-152's eligibility (it exists in no GDD today), and both frames of every lie-capable `mach_*` sheet sit on one sheet page. The Presenter reads the Graph for *which honest frame*, never for a displayed value. The **state glyph** is the same function: an 8x8 chamfered-square lens mark on the module housing with two frames of different *shape* (run: a filled lens with a 2-px inner tick; stop: a hollow lens with a 2-px diagonal bar) so they survive the hue-removed and greyscale tests; it carries no loop hue, no flow mark and no fitting silhouette (ART 8.2: an 8x8 mark never identifies a loop), and a glyph lie swaps to the other honest glyph frame *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's 8x8 shape-coded lens adopted over the ux-designer's 16x16 hue-while-running glyph; a hue swap beside a possibly lying needle is an oracle and fact 14 reserves 16x16 for HUD glyphs)*. No other sprite of the same module may draw the honest state beside an override; a WORN patch plate is a separate TRUTH-graded sprite (a lie that cracks a whole machine over a patch plate is a content lint case for Derelict Authoring, `PATCH_OVER_OVERRIDE`). (advisor ruling R7; PF-45, SN:1346)
*Why.* A SPRITE_SWAP lie is only fair if both frames are ordinary state tokens the player has seen.
*Edge notes.* ART 7.2 / 8.9 line 12 ("icons never swap to express state") needs an exemption for reading surfaces whose lie *is* a frame choice (state glyph, machine frames): bible refresh BR-1, the art-director's. Direction of change: the frame follows the same Graph value the audio reads (IW-32). Stage-3 machine frames and the stage-2 lamp-housing pair are the cuttable tier (IW-34).

**IW-18. WORN and patched presentation.**
*Rule.* A WORN subject (DEGRADED, no hazard mode, `medium` NONE, `acoustic` NONE; LS-11) shows module-body wear: the wear overlay frame (scuffs, and a visible patch plate if patched) on the machine and on the instrument bound to it; the gauge shows the perceived reading of the module's output as usual. No word, bar, rating, colour grade or numeral says "worn" (BS-6, IA-39). A patched subject is permanently DEGRADED `sev` 1 (LS-10, D.4) and keeps its patch plate; the plate is driven by the node's patched state (`hp_cap < HP_FULL`; the Graph's PATCH_WEEP id 27 row uses the same condition and draws the weep on the consequence channel, which Instruments never touch) and not by the WORN descriptor *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Failure & Trail draws nothing for WORN (FT:232, :637). The wear overlay is corruptible only through the machine-frame swap at stage 3 (a false-fixed scrubber looks whole while its witness says otherwise); it is honest at stages 0-2. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6 GAP: the Module-Body Presenter owns the patch plate, so it gains the D39 bead axis that Interaction D.1b needs and that Failure & Trail cannot draw, FT-32 row 27 being one static POINT_FIXED mark with no length axis.)* **Patch-plate bead.** The patch plate carries a weld bead of 1, 2 or 3 segments (user-confirmed default D39, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20); registry `bead_segments`, owner Interaction D.1b): the Presenter selects one of three bead frames of the plate overlay by `bead_segments(h) = clamp(1 + floor(2 * (h - LEAK_HP) / (PATCH_CAP_BP - LEAK_HP)), 1, 3)` with h = the subject's true `hp` from the Graph (LS-19: `node_hp(id)`, or the `hp` field of `edge(id)` for an edge). At registry defaults (`LEAK_HP` 4000, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000, span 2000): hp 4000-499
*Why.* Routed thread 5; BS-6 and IA-39: no condition surface.
*Edge notes.* Wear frames are authored once per module sheet, never per loose item (AD-BS-5 forbids a per-loose-item wear set as "the inspect card in disguise"). WORN is shown here on module-body surfaces only; the card shows no wear (IW-22). LS-11 (mode 10 WORN: "readable on the sprite, the gauge and the inspect card") and LSG:168 are read as: WORN reaches the card only through the module's reduced output reading; the card carries no wear frame, word or mark (advisor ruling R2).

**IW-19. The in-world alarm mark: TRUTH-graded, on the housing, alarm-eligible only.**
*Rule.* While the bound subject has an `alarm_eligible` failure descriptor (LS-13; severity >= 3; read through `failures(filter)`), an instrument housing that can carry it shows one Alarm Red `#E0102A` chamfered-square warning mark (ART:817 shape, ART 7.2 canonical size 16x16 art px, `ALARM_MARK_WORLD_PX` 16, "nothing smaller") on the **housing, not the face**. The world twin's exclamation stroke is **Void Steel**, not Paper White (Paper White is UI-only, fact 16, ART 4.6; the HUD twin keeps Paper White). **Where the mark may be drawn (stage-12 CD-GDD-ALIGN concern 1, P4 cost rule; rewritten 2026-10-27 as a decision table).** The mark is drawn only on a housing that is physically at the alarm-eligible subject. That is a property of placement data (`mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node`, IW-8) and not of a tag: the decision table below lists every case. An instrument with `hops(mount_room, subject_room)` >= 1 (REMOTE) satisfies none of the yes rows, so the lethal remote FALSE_OK of Beat C is never put beside its own contradiction by a lit Alarm Red mark on the lying instrument's housing, and believing the mark still costs a walk to where the subject is (P4: checking costs time, risk or trust). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The mark itself stays TRUTH-graded and untagged; this rule decides only on which housings it is drawn, from authored placement data (`mount_room`, `subject_room`, `host_node` and the binding), never from a lie state. The mark lives on a DIAL_L housing meeting that test (in the 36 px horizontal bay beside the 60x46 housing), on machine and console panels and on the tank prop meeting it; **DIAL_S carries none** *(orchestrator ruling: the art-director's narrowing adopted over the ux-designer's 4-row overlap of the DIAL_S arc; a 16x16 mark ca
*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **IW-19 decision table (housing, mount, binding, `hops`).** A mark also requires an `alarm_eligible` descriptor on the bound subject (above); the table decides only whether the housing may carry one.

I'm checking whether IW's gleam/motion rules actually cover static-pair frames, since IW only describes it generically — static pairs have no needle, the frame stays fixed via frame_override, and I need to figure out where motion_mode gets recorded for numeral-only STALE readouts.

For the BREATH row, PF already pairs STALE with a breathing gleam driven by leak_amplitude_pm, so I'll set motion_mode to STALE while letting the gleam amplitude breathe. I'll add the BREATH row to IW-13 and S2 specifying frame_override holds the frame still, the gleam breathes via leak_amplitude_pm, and there's no needle motion, settle, or tremor — plus a brief note that numeral-only STALE readouts still carry the breathing gleam since instruments draw leak_amplitude_pm in every mode.

Static-pair frames like housing and glyph have no needle, so tremor_weight_pm is technically carried but unused there — honest tremor only applies on the DIAL/LINEAR needle ref, distinct from the housing_glow ref, and card parity means the card uses the same ref and weight. I need IW-5 to explicitly name tremor_weight_pm as the honest tremor's weight alongside displayed_pm, and introduce an env_latch scalar that captures the timestamp of the first non-HONEST frame so the presenter can track tremor state transitions properly.

For the precise freeze formula: once mode leaves HONEST, env is frozen at env_L, the value from the last HONEST frame — no new rise, no predicate reads. The offset o is computed by scaling amplitude by TREMOR_GAIN, env_L, a fade function s(t), and w (weight/1000), clamped to ±A_eff; both env_L and w fading linearly means the product fades over TREMOR_BLEND_S, and rounding causes the offset to vanish to exactly zero once amplitude drops below 0.5, at which point the tremor state is discarded and the flag cleared.

I'm choosing to freeze rather than let it decay naturally, since that's simpler and still conservative under the Filter's blend rule, and the presenter must avoid reading the predicate during non-HONEST frames so tremors never restart mid-lie (AC-PF-46). When mode returns to HONEST, w resets to 1000 and the discarded state means the predicate starts a fresh onset ramp from zero — consistent with no tremor being in progress — and since lie durations vastly exceed the 1s blend window, w will always have reached zero before CLEAR. I also need to confirm this holds the same whether the card is open or closed when the lie begins, and account for hard_start behavior.

At restore, the tremor state clears and w depends purely on the ledger's lie_tau — if a lie is already past the blend window, w is zero and there's no tremor to show, but if restore happens mid-blend, the presenter has no env_L since it was cleared, so output stays zero even though w is nonzero, which correctly ensures no tremor ever starts fresh. I'm now updating the dispatch table's Tremor column across modes: HONEST shows tremor only if the predicate is active; GLIDE/TICK/STALE/RETURN only fade out an already-running tremor via tremor_weight_pm and never start new ones; BREATH has none since there's no needle. I also need to check the Notch column, which clears immediately in these modes.

For reduced motion, the notch still clears instantly at lie onset — this is a known tell similar to the tremor-stopping issue, but the instructions explicitly say to keep this behavior immediate rather than blending it, so I'll note it as an accepted residual limitation rather than change it, and I'll update AC-IW-44 to mention that under RM, with tremor suppressed, there's nothing left to fade anyway. Now I'm defining the updated output formula for section D.5, combining tremor gain, effective amplitude, envelope, and the scaled tremor weight into a clamped rounded value.

I'm adding new variable rows for tremor_weight_pm and the TREMOR_BLEND_S placeholder, defining env_L as a latched envelope that freezes at the last honest value and never rises during non-HONEST frames, and refining the output range description so it's exactly zero only once tremor_weight_pm reaches zero (within the blend window). I'm also walking through a worked numeric example at frame k=1 and a half-second-later case to verify the rounding behavior stays consistent with the formula.

Tracking the fade-out time more precisely: with A_eff=2 the tremor stays visible until about 0.833 s, and with A_eff=1 it fades by around 0.667 s, both safely bounded within the 1.0 s TREMOR_BLEND_S window. I'm double-checking the rounding condition (round-half-away-from-zero) against the maximum envelope and swing values to confirm these thresholds, and now considering how a weaker env_L mid-onset would shrink these times further, plus whether index clamping at the end stops introduces any edge cases.

Now I'm drafting the behavior spec for what happens when the Filter flips from HONEST to a lying state mid-settle — the settle triple and notch clear immediately, the needle snaps to the raw displayed value, but any already-running tremor isn't cleared; instead it continues riding on env_L with its weight preserved at the flip frame so there's no visual jump, then linearly fades to zero over the blend window, layered on top of the Filter's output. I'm also writing the companion rule for when the stress predicate is active while the reading is lying: no new tremor or notch appears since the predicate isn't evaluated outside honest frames, any tremor already in progress simply fades out per the above, and afterward the gauge sits still while the lie's other signals (gleam, restless motion, sound) continue.

For the brief window right at a tremor's blend-out, I'm noting that a lying needle could still shake faintly for under a second, which isn't a contradiction of the rule since it's a leftover fade rather than a freshly triggered tremor — the key guarantee is the lie never *starts* a new one. I'm also adding a small clause for when a lie ends: the first honest frame afterward has no settle since there's no jump, and the tremor state resets cleanly so the stress predicate can restart its onset ramp if stress still holds.

Now I'm updating the summary table row for filter-driven transitions to reflect this clearing/fading behavior and expanding the list of lying states to include BREATH, with a note on how BREATH's static-pair framing interacts with the override.

I'm refining the language around tremor as a flag — clarifying that it can only be freshly started during honest or settling frames, never during a lying one, though an already-running tremor can continue fading. I'm also tightening the exit condition for non-honest modes: the flag transitions into a fading state with no new onset, using the frozen gain envelope, and clears once its weight hits zero or on a hard restart or reset. I'm updating the transition table entry to reflect that the settle triple and notch clear on these honest-to-lying transitions, while a running tremor persists through its fade rather than being cleared outright, and updating the matching invariant statement to capture that the tremor flag can coexist with a lying mode only while mid-fade with a frozen envelope.

Now I'm going through a list of other line references across the document that need consistency checks — several rows discussing the honest-only tremor rule, a forbidden-state row, and a quoted invariant from another section that may need a note about the weight-based amendment. I'm planning to pull up each of these locations in turn and also search for related terminology variants to make sure nothing was missed.

**What must never happen (named as rule violations).** An honest gauge that glides; a lying gauge that settles or trembles; a card that disagrees with its gauge in either direction; a lie that ends with a snap or a cue (the end is never announced, SN-16); any surface that lets a player read their sanity off an instrument (a gauge that always lies near a stage threshold, a colour correlated with stage; PF-38).

| E5 | Stress predicate begins / ends (IW-12) | tremor ramps in over `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` 150 and decays over `TREMOR_DECAY_MS` 600, resting on a pixel | none | honest-only | tremor on a lying reading; tremor with no predicate |

| E6 | Lie begins (Filter) | the needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim (slew plus wander) from the current drawn angle; the gleam fades up with `leak_amplitude_pm` | the Filter's `FA_LIE_SIG_GAUGE` (needle, card, glyph) or `FA_LIE_SIG_SPRITE` (housing, machine), starting no later than the glide | corruptible | any settle or tremor on the lying instrument; a sound-only lie |

| Stress notch, tremor | honest-only presentation of a Graph predicate | none (a `read_view` predicate) | never on a lying reading | none | absent when `motion_mode` is not HONEST |
Honest tremor and the reduced-motion stress notch appear only on an honest reading (R9, R19), so "shake = real" is a rule the game never breaks. Under reduced motion the lie stays distinguishable: never-rest and the continuous digit tick remain, glide scaling is the Filter's (PF-39), settle becomes a step, tremor becomes a held notch that is never shown on a lying reading.
*Edge notes.* The card has no module-frame surface, so if the wall shows a stage-3 `whole` frame while the module is `cracked`, the card shows only the reading and there is nothing for it to disagree with. Stress is the one honest-only difference of *form* that may arise (tremor versus the held notch under `reduced_motion`, K-18 resolved by D96); it is honest-only on both and never differs in a lie *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
**IW-26. Card parity: the same instrument, not a second one.**
*Rule.* The card uses the **same** `PerceptionRef` as its wall gauge (there is no card ref and no card lie), reads the same `Perceived` through the same memo, shows the same drawn value (it reads the instrument's own settle triple and tremor state), the same motion mode, the same gleam parameters and the same HR-5 tri-modal tell, from stage 1. A lie that starts, ends or changes while the card is open appears on the card in the same frame as on the wall gauge, with no flash of the true value. Closing and reopening a card on an active lie shows the same `Perceived` and plays no new sound (the sound is the Filter's request on the ref, not on the card). Opening the card never replays a settle and never sweeps the needle in from zero. "Second instrument" in P4 is always a *different* gauge elsewhere, never the card. The card dial renders the same angle set as the wall needle (it must not be a more precise render of a lying value than the wall is of the same value). The card numeral is `displayed_value` of the **same** `.needle` ref's `Perceived` (checkpoint ruling C2): it is not a second lie target and carries no `lie_surface_id` of its own. In every non-HONEST mode the card needle draws `displayed_pm` verbatim (the Filter's trajectory, wander included, which never rests), while TICK (continuous tick) and STALE (held digits) govern the numeral only, so the card and the wall gauge never disagree about which motion mode is active (PF-9, PF-18, AC-PF-23; HR-14).

input.notes: The single blocker is a CONFLICT: Perception Filter is the publisher and registry source of Perceived (ten fields, including tremor_weight_pm, and the BREATH motion_mode; PF-8 L266/L270, PF-17 L349, L335/L554, registry L1411). Instruments never mention either and say 'tremor cleared that frame' and 'exactly 0 in every non-HONEST frame', which cannot pass together with AC-PF-46/85. Under G1 all edits land in in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view; no sibling GDD needs to change. The design choice made explicit in the requests: on the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches env_hold (the env of the last HONEST frame), stops reading the predicate, and lets tremor_weight_pm alone carry the fade, so o = clamp(round(1.5 x A_eff x env_hold x s x tremor_weight_pm/1000), -A_eff, +A_eff). Letting the predicate go false and decaying env over 600 ms would kill the visible tremor in about 0.3 s and leave about 0.7 s of near-stillness at lie onset, which is the onset-rest problem PF-17 exists to prevent. Recomputed bounds at registry defaults (TREMOR_BLEND_S := WANDER_ONSET_S 1.0 s): the last possible non-zero frame is t = 1.0 x (1 - 1/(3 x A_eff)) = 0.667 s at A_eff 1 and 0.833 s at A_eff 2, and no 2-px frame occurs after 0.5 s; AC thresholds are tremor_weight_pm <= 166 (A_eff 2) and <= 333 (A_eff 1) giving o = 0. The settle triple, prev_honest_pm and the reduced-motion notch stay cleared immediately, said explicitly (under reduced motion no tremor is drawn, so nothing fades). BREATH applies only to static-pair refs (glyph, housing glow, machine frame): frame_override held still, gleam breathing through leak_amplitude_pm, no needle, no settle, no tremor; a numeral-only READOUT lie is STALE with a breathing gleam, not BREATH. Requests also cover every copy of the old prohibition wording (L104, L106, L569, L1253, L1399, VA-8 E5/E6, VA-9, X-2), I-2, S2/S4, I-A and IW-5, card parity IW-26/IW-27, the Tuning Knobs cited row for TREMOR_BLEND_S, and a G3 confirming grep sweep. Registry mirror (not a target in the enum, so carried inside the X-5 request for the registry writer): entities.yaml tremor_offset (source: this GDD) needs the tremor_weight_pm/1000 term in `expression`, the new `output` (currently 'exactly 0 in every non-HONEST frame', about L6512), added variables, and the perceived_query `rules` line 'Instruments apply settle and tremor only when motion_mode is HONEST' (about L1414) reworded. Not requested: PF OQ-PF-42 and E-PF-62 wording (noted only, Filter writer's call) and HUD HS-28 (true as written because the HUD draws no tremor). No R1-R21 ruling bears on this blocker; R13/R14 epoch are not involved.

toolu_01Dz7zrpt1ra9PhdecAttsNJ.notes: The single blocker is a CONFLICT: Perception Filter is the publisher and registry source of Perceived (ten fields, including tremor_weight_pm, and the BREATH motion_mode; PF-8 L266/L270, PF-17 L349, L335/L554, registry L1411). Instruments never mention either and say 'tremor cleared that frame' and 'exactly 0 in every non-HONEST frame', which cannot pass together with AC-PF-46/85. Under G1 all edits land in in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view; no sibling GDD needs to change. The design choice made explicit in the requests: on the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches env_hold (the env of the last HONEST frame), stops reading the predicate, and lets tremor_weight_pm alone carry the fade, so o = clamp(round(1.5 x A_eff x env_hold x s x tremor_weight_pm/1000), -A_eff, +A_eff). Letting the predicate go false and decaying env over 600 ms would kill the visible tremor in about 0.3 s and leave about 0.7 s of near-stillness at lie onset, which is the onset-rest problem PF-17 exists to prevent. Recomputed bounds at registry defaults (TREMOR_BLEND_S := WANDER_ONSET_S 1.0 s): the last possible non-zero frame is t = 1.0 x (1 - 1/(3 x A_eff)) = 0.667 s at A_eff 1 and 0.833 s at A_eff 2, and no 2-px frame occurs after 0.5 s; AC thresholds are tremor_weight_pm <= 166 (A_eff 2) and <= 333 (A_eff 1) giving o = 0. The settle triple, prev_honest_pm and the reduced-motion notch stay cleared immediately, said explicitly (under reduced motion no tremor is drawn, so nothing fades). BREATH applies only to static-pair refs (glyph, housing glow, machine frame): frame_override held still, gleam breathing through leak_amplitude_pm, no needle, no settle, no tremor; a numeral-only READOUT lie is STALE with a breathing gleam, not BREATH. Requests also cover every copy of the old prohibition wording (L104, L106, L569, L1253, L1399, VA-8 E5/E6, VA-9, X-2), I-2, S2/S4, I-A and IW-5, card parity IW-26/IW-27, the Tuning Knobs cited row for TREMOR_BLEND_S, and a G3 confirming grep sweep. Registry mirror (not a target in the enum, so carried inside the X-5 request for the registry writer): entities.yaml tremor_offset (source: this GDD) needs the tremor_weight_pm/1000 term in `expression`, the new `output` (currently 'exactly 0 in every non-HONEST frame', about L6512), added variables, and the perceived_query `rules` line 'Instruments apply settle and tremor only when motion_mode is HONEST' (about L1414) reworded. Not requested: PF OQ-PF-42 and E-PF-62 wording (noted only, Filter writer's call) and HUD HS-28 (true as written because the HUD draws no tremor). No R1-R21 ruling bears on this blocker; R13/R14 epoch are not involved.

requests.change:
1) Replace the final sentence of the Rule by: 'The tremor is STARTED and its predicate is read only when `motion_mode` is HONEST (advisor ruling R9; AT-17, AT:1415 C1). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G1: Perception Filter publishes `tremor_weight_pm` and BREATH, PF-8, PF-17)* **Onset of a lie: a running tremor fades, it does not stop.** Instruments read `tremor_weight_pm` (int 0..1000, the tenth `Perceived` field, PF-8; 1000 on every HONEST frame; read from the same single `perceived()` pull as `displayed_pm`, never computed or cached here). In the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches `env_hold := env` of the last HONEST frame (0 if no tremor was running) and from then on (a) no new tremor starts and no onset ramp runs in any non-HONEST frame (the predicate is not read; a flag cannot be set in a non-HONEST frame), (b) env stays `env_hold` (no rise, no decay of its own; the fade is carried by `tremor_weight_pm` alone), (c) the drawn offset is the D.5 offset multiplied by `tremor_weight_pm / 1000`, which falls linearly from 1000 on the first ACTIVE frame to 0 over `TREMOR_BLEND_S` (Filter-owned, := `WANDER_ONSET_S`, 1.0 s `[PLACEHOLDER]`) and stays 0 until CLEAR, and (d) the flag clears and `env_hold` is discarded when `tremor_weight_pm` reaches 0, on `hard_start`, cull, camera cut and restore (so a restore mid-fade shows no tremor: Instruments never start one), and at the first HONEST frame after the lie (CLEAR): the predicate is then re-read and, if stress still holds, a fresh `TREMOR_ONSET_MS` ramp starts from env 0; `env_hold` is never carried across CLEAR. The **settle triple and the reduced-motion notch are the opposite: they are cleared at once** in the first non-HONEST frame (IW-11 (e), IW-27); under `reduced_motion` the tremor is not drawn, so there is nothing to fade and only the immediate notch clearing applies. Why the fade is `tremor_weight_pm` and not the 600 ms `TREMOR_DECAY_MS`: the tremor fades out over exactly the window in which the Filter\'s wander fades in (`TREMOR_BLEND_S` := `WANDER_ONSET_S`), so the onset second is never still (PF-17, AC-PF-46 bounds the onset rest on this); letting the predicate go false at onset would decay the envelope in about 0.3 s and leave about 0.7 s of near-stillness, and a tremor that stops dead at lie onset is itself a tell.'
2) In the Rule sentence 'Tremor is never driven by Attention, sanity, a timer or a lie.' keep it (a lie never starts or drives a tremor) and add after it: 'A fading tremor is the honest tremor already in progress, not a lie\'s.'
3) In the 'On the card' paragraph, after 'The card shows the same honest tremor as its wall gauge (parity, IW-26;' insert 'the same fade at lie onset, from the same presenter state and the same `tremor_weight_pm`;'.

Under G1 all edits land in in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view; no sibling GDD needs to change. The design choice made explicit in the requests: on the first non-HONEST frame the presenter latches env_hold (the env of the last HONEST frame), stops reading the predicate, and lets tremor_weight_pm alone carry the fade, so o = clamp(round(1.5 x A_eff x env_hold x s x tremor_weight_pm/1000), -A_eff, +A_eff). Letting the predicate go false and decaying env over 600 ms would kill the visible tremor in about 0.3 s and leave about 0.7 s of near-stillness at lie onset, which is the onset-rest problem PF-17 exists to prevent. Recomputed bounds at registry defaults (TREMOR_BLEND_S := WANDER_ONSET_S 1.0 s): the last possible non-zero frame is t = 1.0 x (1 - 1/(3 x A_eff)) = 0.667 s at A_eff 1 and 0.833 s at A_eff 2, and no 2-px frame occurs after 0.5 s; AC thresholds are tremor_weight_pm <= 166 (A_eff 2) and <= 333 (A_eff 1) giving o = 0. The settle triple, prev_honest_pm and the reduced-motion notch stay cleared immediately, said explicitly (under reduced motion no tremor is drawn, so nothing fades). BREATH applies only to static-pair refs (glyph, housing glow, machine frame): frame_override held still, gleam breathing through leak_amplitude_pm, no needle, no settle, no tremor; a numeral-only READOUT lie is STALE with a breathing gleam, not BREATH.
